title: Local shard compositor for per-route/model/customer cost & latency decomposition
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a local "compositor" microservice that consumes streaming usage events and produces deterministic per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency decompositions. The component runs close to the streaming partition (Kafka partition / Kinesis shard) so we can keep attribution state local, perform watermark-based windows, and emit compacted nearline rollups for downstream reconciliation. The compositor is responsible for: 1) assigning deterministic shard keys (route+model+customer hash) and maintaining small in-memory counters and latency histograms; 2) applying the lightweight apportionment function (token-weighted + model-latency model) per request; 3) producing two outputs — immediate nearline rollups for Console dashboards and periodic reconciliation batches for the ledger service; 4) fallback to compact spill-to-storage lanes when memory thresholds are exceeded; 5) exposing diagnostics and explainability metadata (apportionment factors, sample requests) for debugging regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Compositor consumer reads events and emits nearline rollup messages with <5s end-to-end delay under steady load
Deterministic apportionment reproduces nightly batch totals within 0.5% for synthetic workloads
Memory spill path works and preserves eventual consistency after restart
Metrics emitted: per-shard backlog, watermark lag, apportionment variance, sample CPI (cost-per-invocation)
Integration: downstream reconciler (ENG-51102) can consume compositor batches and reconcile with billing ledger
comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket. POC notes in Confluence. Goal: reduce reconciliation churn and provide explainable per-route economics for Console UX.

2026-02-16 Marco Nguyen: Design spike done. Chosen approach: hybrid stream+nearline; use local in-memory state keyed by route|model|customer with periodic flushes. Trade-off: slightly higher memory per consumer vs much lower cross-shard shuffling.
2026-02-19 Design review (Liam O'Connor): Requested explicit explainability fields and a compact sample of representative requests per apportionment bucket. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-02-22 Eng review (Sofia Ramos): Benchmarks on m5.xlarge consumer show ~12k events/s with 64MB working set; need CPU optimizations for high-cardinality tenants. Plan: move histogram to DDSketch and use sampled KV cache references.
2026-02-26 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-analytics/pull/412 (compositor consumer + spill-to-s3 lanes). Awaiting integration tests.

2026-03-01 Marco Nguyen: Integration test failures fixed (race in watermark handling). Nightly reconciliation shows 0.32% delta vs current batch baseline on synthetic load. Ready for canary deployment to analytics-dev.
Next: coordinate canary with infra during 2026-03-05 maintenance window; add alerting for apportionment variance >1% and consumer lag >30s.
notes: Key implementation details: 1) apportionment uses deterministic token-count weighting with an additive latency-adjustment term derived from lightweight model-specific latency profiles; 2) we avoid cross-partition grouping by computing per-shard partials and relying on a nightly reconcilier to assemble final ledgers; 3) spill-to-s3 lane serializes compressed protobuf envelopes and writes index files for fast recloning; 4) we will measure cost delta introduced by the compositor (expected to be ~0.02% of infra spend) and capture it in telemetry. Operational runbooks and DB migration plan are in Confluence link above.
